title: Does this game look/feel fun to play?
author: Diveye
selftext:
I've been working on this game for a while now, and recently started reworking a lot of my previous work with AI. Naturally, things are moving a lot faster, and as I am more capable of reaching my initial idea for this game, I'm also beginning to wonder if the game is going to be as fun as I envisioned it to be. 

In this game, you are a virus sent by humans in a last attempt to deliver an exploit inside a breach deeply rooted within a super AI that has taken over the planet and enslaved humanity.   
  
Any feedback is most welcome!

comments.author: RoboProletariat
comments.body:
The open spaces are significantly more interesting than the tunnels. There might be some way to add creativity to the tunnel bits, but having boring moments can be good in moderation.   
I don't think anybody can judge feel without playing it. The settings of the 'flight model' obviously make or break the game here. 

what are the 'mission failed' states? What are the details of 'mission complete'?  
This feels like a reskin of a popular archetype, which is a lot better than the current AI slop of reskinning a popular title. I think you have a coherent idea here. The 'fun part' will come down to playtesting and tuning the 'rhythm of action' so a player isn't overwhelmed or frustrated with getting lost.

replies.author: Diveye
replies.body:
Those tunnels are actually really hard, and get harder with time too, but I understand that they are not as action packed as the City room which is also shown here. Thanks for pointing that out. 

It's a roguelite approach so death means all progress lost. Misson complete essentially means you passed the level and are moving deeper into the AI. The cool bit is that the AI uses your playstyle against you: you like going fast and not dealing with enemies? More enemies. You like going slow and taking everything down: timers & harder-to-deal-with enemies. Furthermore, rooms actually adapt and so their enemies based on how you complete them.

Nautarally playtesting will make a big impact here.

comments.author: Remarkable_Swing_709
comments.body:
The fighting seems out of place. I think you've used colour correctly as a guide for where you can go/what you're supposed to do (the yellow)

I'd lean into the rhythm/speed of the game. Looks like geometry dash style. You shouldn't really slow down IMO. If you still want directionality with colour and turns where the objective is clearly off screen, you'd better have a clear indicator of where you should be going.

Upon second watch, you didn't quite use colour at the start as the objective. It seems like you're internally clashing between free choice directionality and locked choice.

What I would change: all checkpoints the same colour (yellow) remove "options" I saw you go through a purple ring that was just confusing a little. Remove fighting altogether. Add more red hazards. More frequent yellow rings, and remove brakes so you can't slow down.

If you wanted to lean more into the fighting I'd just make a different mode for something like that.

replies.author: Diveye
replies.body:
This is one of my concerns too. So essentially there are two ways to play the game: either as a super high speed virus that zooms through the levels, but is more fragile and has less firepower, or as a heavy virus that is slower, bulkier and better armed, or anything in between. The player has total freedom over how they build and orient their ship to match their playstyle, down to the the types of guns and equipments they want to put on it, so that they can really fine tune their experience to how they want to play the game. It's the AI's role to adapt to that playstyle accordingly, making sure levels remain challenging by playing on the player's weaknesses, all the while the player is given great choices to further fine tune their playing style with items in the game. 

Do you think this could work? 

For the color feedback totally agree. I'll have another pass on that thank you :)
